description: Acceptance for the proven native Intel AU endpoint publication defect. A scheduled normalized Float32 endpoint must survive host readback without an additional physical Float32 round trip. The original host-automation.json predicates and limits are unchanged.

au_normalized_publication.truth: An accepted scheduled value and its current physical-storage readback are distinct representations. In the modern circuit policy, GetParameter returns the accepted normalized Float32 endpoint while that publication still owns the parameter. A direct setter, UI/state notification, lifecycle reset or changed actual storage readback invalidates that ownership. Untouched parameters and Pure/Legacy return their original parameter getter value. No physical parameter mapping or audio trajectory changes.
witnesses: For every named key, schedule explicit Float32 immediate values and ramps ending at a transmitted Float32 knot on the current render's final sample. Native AudioUnitGetParameter must return that accepted Float32 exactly. Include the native failing pulse-width value 0.62851631641387939, additional interior values, and endpoints zero and one. This exact knot check supplements, and does not replace, the original 1e-7 double-interpolated endpoint test.

Compile the production AU hook body against a parameter fixture whose getter deliberately models a nonidentity physical Float32 round trip. Verify exact accepted scheduled readback, original storage values before any publication, changed-storage fallback, and invalidation even when the storage readback itself is unchanged.

A later native offset-zero setter and restored state supersede a previously scheduled endpoint. Use exact range endpoints where an independent native oracle is required, so the test does not assume arbitrary physical Float32 inversion is exact.

Initialization, reset and cleanup discard publication ownership. UI/state notifications and direct setters invalidate only the affected key; unsupported parameters keep their original adapter behavior.
Pure and Legacy always retain their original storage-based readback and existing audio/offset behavior, even when a prior modern scheduled endpoint remains in publication storage.

Retain every existing native AU scheduling, audio partition, capacity, invalid-input, future-endpoint, Pure/Legacy, factory/memory and sixteen-voice assertion unchanged. Native Intel must pass; arm64 success alone does not qualify the defect.
mutations: Bypass normalized publication and return the physical-storage getter; the exact knot publication gate and native Intel original endpoint gate must reject it.
Retain publication ownership after invalidation, or return a cached endpoint despite a changed underlying getter; the external-state ownership witness must reject it.
Use normalized publication under Pure/Legacy; the protected readback witness must reject it.
Suppress lifecycle publication reset; the reset ownership witness must reject it.
au_normalized_publication.registration_order: Publish this file before evaluating new witnesses or a production repair. First record the original-code failure, then the repaired result and isolated mutations. Preserve all original thresholds.

native_before.diagnosis: Only the affine pulse-width ranges fail. Every printed actual readback equals the independently calculated normalized-to-physical-Float32-to-normalized-Float32 projection exactly; all 64 expected/actual physical projections also agree. This proves publication loss, not incorrect ramp timing or a nonlinear libm hypothesis. The physical numbers are projections, not direct hardware or internal-storage measurements.

Declared software inference: the normalized value already accepted by the scheduled host protocol remains authoritative until a later parameter edit or lifecycle boundary supersedes it. This is not a CS-80 circuit law.
